  Requirement: "Each attempt now gives the model a fresh copy of the captured index through `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and the script still stages and commits the accepted resolution itself." (PR description; restated in `changelog.d/5627-resolver-private-model-index.md:4`.)
  Expected change site: `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` — the `stage_resolver_touched_path_or_fail` function definition at line 44.
  Evidence of absence: The round 1 fix added a comment at the post-loop block (around line 2940 in the new file) explaining that staging runs on the real index on purpose, but the function definition at line 44 carries no such comment. The function runs `git add` / `git rm` (lines 49, 54) on whatever index the calling process has, lives before the source-repo gating and before `RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE` is defined, and is only documented by the function's own name. A future editor who refactors this function or wraps its call in a subshell that exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE=${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}` would silently reintroduce the original failure mode: the resolution would stage into the private copy, the real index would keep its unmerged entries, and the merge commit would carry nothing. `test_private_model_index_wiring` asserts loop-level wiring but does not pin the function definition's contract. The round 1 fixer comment (entry 5912425635) explicitly addresses only the post-loop block, not the function definition.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Evidence of absence: The round 1 fix added a comment at the post-loop staging block (around line 2870 in the new file, after the 3-line comment is inserted) explaining that staging runs on the real index and must not set `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. However, the function definition itself (lines 44-63) carries no such documentation. The function calls `git add` and `git rm` which operate on the calling process's current index, but a reader who finds the function by itself has no signal that it must run on the real index. A future editor who refactors this function or wraps its call in a subshell that exports `GIT_INDEX_FILE=${RESOLVER_MODEL_INDEX_FILE}` would silently reintroduce the original failure mode: the resolution would be staged into the private copy, the real index would still have unmerged entries, and the merge commit would carry nothing. The test `test_private_model_index_wiring` asserts loop-level wiring but does not pin that the function definition itself stays on the real index. The reviewer consensus in round 1 (minimax, qwen) flagged this exact site; the fix comment (entry 5912425635) only mentioned the post-loop block.
